extracted.intended_audience: speakers, organizers, and reporters preparing Oberwolfach Reports (mathematicians submitting extended abstracts and compiling reports)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing, formatting, and submitting Oberwolfach Reports: organizers write an introduction and collect extended abstracts from speakers; a reporter compiles the LaTeX source and submits the report to the MFO. Covers content, structure, formatting, timeline, and copyright.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of OWR
rubrics_metrics.description: The Oberwolfach Reports (OWR) contain extended abstracts of the talks given at every Workshop, Mini-Workshop, or Arbeitsgemeinschaft (study group) in Oberwolfach; aim is to report periodically upon the state of mathematical research and make these reports available to the mathematical community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OWR are official, quotable documents used to refer to results, open problems, and new developments; they are published quarterly in hardcover and electronically and distributed to services like zbMATH Open and Mathematical Reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which contributions are included
rubrics_metrics.description: Each report should include the extended abstracts of the talks given during the meeting and an introduction written by the organizers. Abstracts or research reports from participants who did not give a talk are not included as a rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage inclusion of open questions and conjectures; added references should provide necessary background and point to related papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and content of extended abstracts
rubrics_metrics.description: The extended abstracts should keep an informal style and reflect eventually the provisional status of the presented results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to include open questions and conjectures to promote new research problems; include references that provide background and related work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heading information required
rubrics_metrics.description: A heading, giving the exact title and date of the workshop as well as the number of the report, names and affiliated cities of the organizers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please also insert the MRID and/or the ORCID of the organizers in the fields provided for this purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizers' short abstract and MSC
rubrics_metrics.description: A short abstract contributed by the organizers (about 5 lines) and the standard 2020 mathematics subject classification (not more than 10 numbers of the first two digits for the primary classification, please).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract together with the table of contents will be sent by the MFO to zbMATH Open and Mathematical Reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizers' introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: An introduction contributed by the organizers of 1-3 pages, with some information on the topic and the course of the workshop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A summary of the specific areas that were discussed, the main results and most important new developments would be appreciated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A table of contents containing titles and speakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This will be created automatically by the template/class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended abstract length and components
rubrics_metrics.description: The extended abstracts (1-3 pages) of all talks including the title, the speaker, and references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure each extended abstract includes the title, speaker name, and references; adhere to the informal style and note provisional results and open questions when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional session summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional: Summaries of problem or discussion sessions or other activities, if applicable (at most 3 pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include only when relevant; adhere to the page limit for optional material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter name
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of the reporter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the reporter's name in the report metadata as requested by the template.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant list
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of participants including postal addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This will be added by the MFO; do not try to recreate the official participant list yourself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The report should be written in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All contributions and the introduction must be in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total report page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The total amount of pages should not exceed 60 for a Workshop and 25 for a Mini-Workshop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure combined length of introduction, extended abstracts, optional summaries, etc. stays within the appropriate limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image file format and credit
rubrics_metrics.description: If you include any images in your abstract, please use eps-files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you use pictures from others, ensure you are entitled to use them and give all necessary credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of official LaTeX templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors and the reporter are urged to use the electronic LaTeX 2e templates (template for authors and template for reporters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Template consists of a tex file with main structure and a class file; both files must be in the same folder and the template is available at the provided URL. Further instructions will be provided within the template.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not change the class file
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not permitted to change the class file as this is also important to create the right page numbering and table of contents of our hard cover book series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any content as well as individually needed commands and packages should be added to the tex file, not by editing the class file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not change main tex structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not change the main structure of the tex file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the provided talk environment and main file organization instead of restructuring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not change page layout or main font
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not change the page layout or the main font.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve the visual and pagination consistency required for the printed series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid non-standard macros and fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not make use of non-standard macro packages or of special fonts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard packages only to avoid compilation or typesetting problems and incompatibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use provided talk environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Take advantage of the provided talk environment to insert extended abstracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the environment supplied in the template rather than inventing custom formatting for abstracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insert content directly (no includes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter your content directly into the tex-file. Do not use commands like \include or \input to refer to external documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid external file references so the single submitted tex file compiles correctly for the reporter and the MFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define commands safely
rubrics_metrics.description: Make use of \newcommand instead of \renewcommand, \let or \def when defining own commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent overwriting commands of the class file or commands of other authors by using \newcommand; avoid redefining existing macros.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics inclusion and package
rubrics_metrics.description: Include pictures only in .eps-Format using the graphicx-package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure .eps images fit the type area and that you have rights to use external images; give necessary credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use LaTeX structural markups
rubrics_metrics.description: Take advantage of LaTeX-Markups like \section, \subsection, \itemize, \enumerate etc. for structuring and formatting, instead of formatting text manually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper structural markup ensures consistent appearance and correct table of contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AMS theorem environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Take advantage of the AMS theorem environment for theorems instead of formatting theorems manually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard theorem environments for consistent numbering and formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect type area constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Take care, that text, images, formulas, and tables do not exceed the type area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure nothing overflows margins or interferes with pagination and printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use online LaTeX pre-check
rubrics_metrics.description: An online check at https://www.mfo.de/scientific-program/publications/owr/owrdiag is provided to check the LaTeX source for common errors before submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and reporters should use the diagnostic tool to catch common mistakes prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact for template problems
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of any problems with our template, contact reports@mfo.de.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this contact for technical/template issues that cannot be resolved locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speakers' submission timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Speakers are to send extended abstracts of their talks as a LaTeX document by email within four weeks upon completion of the workshop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speakers should also write their abstract (possibly shorter than the extended version) into the book of talks at the meeting; reporters are advised to copy handwritten abstracts if a speaker does not submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizers' role in submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The organizers contribute the introduction together with the abstract and the mathematical subject classification of the workshop and can help the reporter in case any problems arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers should supply MRID/ORCID info and help coordinate collection of abstracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter compilation and quality checks
rubrics_metrics.description: The reporter collects all contributions, puts them together in one file, and ensures that this file compiles without errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporter should fix multiply defined labels and missing references before sending the report; composition should be completed within four weeks after the end of the workshop. Send a tex file with all images to reports@mfo.de.

rubrics_metrics.name: MFO processing and publication workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission, MFO will add the list of participants and publish the report online; after collection of all reports of the quarter they will publish them together in one book issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report will be labeled 'preliminary' until the quarterly book issue with final page numbers is published; final issues appear at the EMS press site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and access
rubrics_metrics.description: The report of an activity can be downloaded from its website (link via annual schedules); direct link will be sent to all participants after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Libraries/institutes can subscribe to OWR on a non-profit basis or make exchange arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and licensing of contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Oberwolfach leaves the copyright of the extended abstracts to the authors. During registration participants are asked to grant a non-exclusive license to the MFO to publish their scientific contribution within the OWR in electronic and printed form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors retain rights to further publish results elsewhere; however, the MFO holds the copyright on OWR as a whole and has the irrevocable right of publication and distribution of the compiled reports.
